Overall: 

I want to examine whether colleges with higher tuition costs have higher graduation rates. Another question I want to explore is whether the average net price students pay has a relationship with graduation rates. 

1. Descriptive Statistics

I plan to calculate basic descriptive statistics, including the mean, median, minimum, and maximum tuition costs and graduation rates. This will help me understand my dataset and identify differences between colleges. 

2. Correlation Tests

I plan to use correlation tests to examine the relationship between tuition costs and graduation rates. I have already started using the cor.test() function in R to examine this relationship. 

3. Scatterplots

I plan to use ggplot() to create scatterplots showing the relationship between tuition and graduation rates. I have already created a basic scatterplot, but I also want to add a trend line to make the relationship easier to understand. 

4. T-Tests

I may use a t-test to determine whether the difference in average graduation rates between public and private nonprofit colleges is statistically significant. 

5. Linear Regression

I also want to try a linear regression model using lm() to examine whether tuition costs help predict graduation rates. 

6. Data Cleaning 

Before completing my analyses, I will check for missing values and make sure the variables are formatted correctly. 

Expected Findings:

I expect to find some relationship between tuition costs and graduation rates, although I am not sure how strong it will be. 



```{r}

```
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

college_data <- read_csv(file.choose())

View(college_data)

names(college_data)
```

```{r}
college_clean <- college_data %>%
  select(INSTNM, CONTROL, TUITIONFEE_IN,
         TUITIONFEE_OUT, NPT4_PUB, NPT4_PRIV,
         C150_4)


college_clean <- college_clean %>%
  rename(
    college = INSTNM,
    type = CONTROL,
    in_state_tuition = TUITIONFEE_IN,
    out_state_tuition = TUITIONFEE_OUT,
    public_net_price = NPT4_PUB,
    private_net_price = NPT4_PRIV,
    graduation_rate = C150_4
  )


View(college_clean)
```

```{r}
college_clean <- college_clean %>%
  mutate(
    college_type = case_when(
      type == 1 ~ "Public",
      type == 2 ~ "Private nonprofit",
      type == 3 ~ "Private for-profit",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
cor.test(college_clean$in_state_tuition,
         college_clean$graduation_rate,
         use = "complete.obs")
```

```{r}
college_clean %>%
  filter(college_type %in% c("Public", "Private nonprofit")) %>%
  group_by(college_type) %>%
  summarise(
    average_graduation = mean(graduation_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    average_tuition = mean(in_state_tuition, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
college_clean <- college_clean %>%
  mutate(
    net_price = case_when(
      type == 1 ~ public_net_price,
      type == 2 ~ private_net_price,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
cor.test(college_clean$net_price,
         college_clean$graduation_rate,
         use = "complete.obs")
```

```{r}
ggplot(college_clean, aes(x = in_state_tuition,
                          y = graduation_rate)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Does Higher Tuition Mean Higher Graduation Rates?",
    x = "Tuition and Fees ($)",
    y = "Six-Year Graduation Rate"
  )
```

```{r}
ggplot(college_clean, aes(x = college_type,
                          y = graduation_rate)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Graduation Rates at Public and Private Colleges",
    x = "College Type",
    y = "Six-Year Graduation Rate"
  )
```
